figures.finding: Employment income is taxed on monthly bands: nothing to RWF 60,000, 10% to 100,000, 20% to 200,000 and 30% above; the same rates apply to residents and non-residents; there are no local income taxes.
figures.applies: Individuals; residents on worldwide income, non-residents on Rwandan-source income The law's annual scale (Art. 14, Table 2, from the second year after the law's commencement) is RWF 0-720,000 0%, to 1,200,000 10%, to 2,400,000 20%, above 30%, the monthly bands times twelve; the May 2025 amending law leaves Art. 14 unchanged.

figures.finding: The tax period is the calendar year; annual returns are due by 31 March of the next year, except for those with only employment income, turnover under RWF 2 million, or (non-residents) income fully subject to withholding.

sources.said: Annual tax returns/declarations for individuals are due by 31 March of the following year after the tax period.
Non-resident individuals who suffer WHT on income sourced from Rwanda.

figures.finding: Everyone working in Rwanda, foreigners included, contributes to the RSSB: pension 6% employee and 6% employer of gross salary (7% each from 2027, rising to 10% each by 2030), occupational hazards 2% employer, maternity 0.3% each, and community health insurance 0.5% of the employee's net salary.

All people working in Rwanda, both nationals and foreigners, are required to contribute to a national social security contribution fund managed by the Rwanda Social Security Board (RSSB).

figures.finding: Employers withhold PAYE monthly and remit it by the 15th of the next month; payers withhold 15% from service fees, royalties and performance payments to an artist or musician where the payee is unregistered or has no recent income tax declaration.

sources.said: Tax on employment income is withheld by the employer under the Pay-As-You-Earn (PAYE) system and remitted to the RRA on a monthly basis together with PAYE returns by the 15th day of the following month.

The WHT is due where such payments or other methods of extinguishing an obligation are made to a person not registered with the tax administration or to a registered person who does not have recent income tax declaration.

figures.finding: A non-resident performer has 15% withheld from performance payments (and 15% on royalties and service fees), and a non-resident whose Rwandan income all bore withholding files no return.

sources.said: Performance payments made to a crafts person, a musician, an artist, or a player in sports, cultural, or leisure activities, irrespective of whether paid directly or indirectly.

figures.finding: VAT is 18%; registration is required at taxable turnover of RWF 20 million in a year or RWF 5 million in a calendar quarter; supplies by unregistered persons bear no VAT.

sources.said: The threshold for VAT registration is taxable turnover of RWF 20 million in any relevant year or RWF 5 million in a calendar quarter. The standard VAT rate is 18%
